title: radar state.json v1
description: The versioned snapshot contract. Consumers (radar CLI, /api/radar/state, the Radar tab, external brief consumers) read ONLY this shape. Additive changes keep v:1; any removal or retype bumps v.

sources.description: Metadata is ALWAYS fresh, even when the data fragment was carried forward from the last good scan (spec §3).

handoffsLive.description: p6: handoffs.length — the ONE count p6 adds. Every p5 count is computed BEFORE suppression (spec §6.6).

inbox.description: p9 (spec §5.4): inbox.length — from the LIST, never from a display array. Present in properties but NOT in required, so snapshots predating p9 (the committed fixtures among them) stay valid.

workRefs.description: p11: OPTIONAL — absent from `required` so a pre-p11 snapshot still validates. Counted from the source list, never from a folded view.

workRefsSelectable.description: p11: OPTIONAL. How many WorkRefs a session could act on right now (spec §6.2).

inbox.description: p9 (spec §5.3/§5.4): every session actually waiting on the operator, oldest-first, uncapped and ungrouped. The ONE derivation that reads the full sessions[] — a vanished session keeps its row (read-only) while every other derivation is shielded from it. Root is closed, so the key must be declared here; it is NOT in root.required, so pre-p9 snapshots stay valid.

handoffs.description: p6 (spec §4.6): ONLY handoffs that hold fact keys — the live set. Terminal handoffs are absent entirely; they live in the ledger. Consumed by the derivation for suppression, never rendered.

handoffRecovery.description: p6 (spec §M4): ONE object for the WHOLE undecidable set, or null. No ids, no count, no array — REQUIRED so a consumer's `!== null` predicate can never fire on an omitted key (undefined !== null).

role.description: p6 (spec §3): published from config.role by derive(); a viewer's OWN proxy overwrites it to "viewer" on the response — the only field the proxy rewrites. The tab renders no select affordance when it reads viewer.

jiraDrift.description: Weekly digest material (spec §M4). NEVER an interrupt and never an attention item — a Jira status that git cannot corroborate belongs here, not on the board.

workRefs.description: p11 (spec §4.1): canonical, source-neutral work references. ADDITIVE and OPTIONAL — absent from `required` on purpose, so a snapshot taken before p11 still validates. status.native/nativeCategory are the source's authority; status.canonical is radar's projection and is never written back. A consumer that assumes this key is present is the defect, not the snapshot that omits it.

status.description: The LIVE statuses only (spec §4.1.1). resolved/abandoned/discarded never appear here — a terminal handoff is absent from state.json.

eventsStatus.description: S-004: hook-event availability, INDEPENDENT of the bridge. The leader reads its own events off disk, so its bridge can be down while its events are current.

stale.description: S-004: this machine's session facts are carried forward from the last good sweep, not re-observed.

statusTruncated.description: S-004a: the bridge's 60-tab list-status cap bit. Tabs past it carry status `unknown` and are still listed — a missing status is never a green.

urn.description: urn:work:<source>:<sourceId> — stable across scans by construction.

native.description: The source's own word, verbatim. This is the authority.

route.description: Resolved once per scan (spec §6.3) so every consumer reads one answer. Null means unresolved, and the reason travels with it.

boards.description: p11: OPTIONAL per-source counter (jiraAgile). Descriptive; no consumer branches on it.

pending.description: p11: OPTIONAL. Work observed but not intaken because a bound was hit — reported so truncation is never silent.

unpushed.description: rev-list --count <branch> --not --remotes. null = the count could not be taken (unknown, never 0).

noRemote.description: true = the branch has no configured upstream. Does NOT change the unpushed algorithm.

branch.description: null for a detached HEAD worktree.

cleanupCommand.description: A command STRING for a human to run. Radar never executes it and never removes a branch.

pushed.description: Named `pushed`, never `built`: the cell may only claim what git proves.

zone.description: gone epics are absent from epics[] entirely.

session.description: CLOSED (p11 D10). The def previously declared 9 of the 22 fields a publisher can emit and left the door open, so the two idle bounds and the identity the resume resolver reads — worktree, lastEventAt, lastSubmitAt — were undeclared AND a typo in any of them was unfalsifiable. Closing it is only safe because every reachable publisher field is now declared; the three publishers are mod-sessions' publish site (the row literal, plus `vanished` when true, plus the events-outage carry-forward which re-emits published rows with stale:true), classify's in-place mutation of that same array between the module loop and derive (collector.js §5.2.6 — derive publishes the fragment array verbatim as state.sessions, so lastAssistant/sessionTitle/intent ride along), and derive's own `branch` enrichment. Fields stay OPTIONAL — `required` is still just key+status — so a pre-p11 snapshot still validates.

worktree.description: p11 D10: the session's ABSOLUTE cwd path, as mapCwd resolved it (mod-sessions ~209 returns `target`, an absolute trimmed cwd — never a branch name and never a relative tail). Identity is NOT matched on this field: links-matching reads the derived `branch`, and the old worktree-specificity tie-break is deleted (D8). Non-null ONLY when `repo` is non-null: mapCwd returns all-null or {repo, worktree, epic} together, so repo-set-with-worktree-null is unreachable and a fixture carrying it is drift (D11).

branch.description: p11: the git branch checked out at `worktree`, joined at derive time from the repo's worktree records. Null when the session has no worktree, when no worktree record matches the path, or when that worktree is on a detached HEAD.

lastEventAt.description: p11 D10: ISO timestamp of the newest hook event for this session. The resume resolver's idle clock is measured from HERE (eligibility.js :: idleMsOf), and a session with no parseable value is refused as `no-clock` rather than treated as fresh — no clock means freshness cannot be proven.

lastSubmitAt.description: p11 D10: ISO timestamp of the last UserPromptSubmit. The resume tie-break sorts on it, newest first (eligibility.js :: tieBreak), so a non-deterministic value here would make a wrong-target incident unreproducible. Also the basis for cacheExpiresAt.

lastStopAt.description: When this session's turn last ENDED — the moment it started waiting. Projected onto inbox rows so a queue of waiting sessions can be ordered.

blockedSince.description: ISO timestamp the session began waiting on the operator; null unless status is blocked. Half of the turn-identity token a reply must echo.

transcriptPath.description: Secondary identity (latest event wins), never primary — identity is {machine, sessionId}. Null when no event carried one.

stale.description: This row was carried forward from the last good sweep rather than re-observed (the events-outage branch). Re-deriving from nothing would clear every block on the machine, which would read as "the operator answered everything".

vanished.description: The session is still blocked but its recorded tab has left the tree. Present ONLY when true, so a consumer that never heard of it sees the row it always saw. Published (carry-forward is rebuilt from published rows) but shielded: every p5 derivation reads liveSessions, and only buildInbox reads the full list — a closed tab removes the Jump, it does not answer the prompt.

lastAssistant.description: Attached in place by the classify stage for blocked rows: {text, ts} of the last assistant turn, or null. The inbox projects it into `question`/`turn.assistantTs`; it is declared here because derive publishes the classifier's own array verbatim.

sessionTitle.description: Attached in place by the classify stage: {text, source} where source is custom (an explicit rename — authoritative) or ai (the automatic titler), or null. Projected onto inbox rows as title/titleSource.

intent.description: Attached in place by the classify stage for blocked rows. WIDER than inboxItem.intent on purpose: offer-more and status-only are real verdicts here and are filtered out by buildInbox, so the queue only ever shows the two that reach it.

model.description: null on every unknown path; a successful verdict must never write that null.

surfaceReason.description: Why the surface join produced null, from a fixed vocabulary (no-cwd, shared-cwd, no-workspace-for-cwd, ambiguous-workspace, no-terminal-tab, ambiguous-tabs:<n>, no-tab-uuid, tree-unavailable, recorded-tab-gone). Null when a surface WAS resolved — including the exact case, where the session recorded its own cmux surface id and the tree confirmed it.

inboxItem.description: p9 (spec §5.3). Closed: the row contract is exact, and a field that leaked in from the source session — `tabStatus` above all — would invite a consumer to read workspace-scoped provenance as per-tab readiness.

cacheApprox.description: Always approximate: the prompt-cache TTL drops to 5 min under overage and radar cannot see which regime it is in.

turn.description: The turn identity token a reply must echo (spec §5.5). blockedSince is the row's own value verbatim.

question.description: The COMPLETE last assistant text, never truncated here; '' when there is none. Truncation is a rendering concern.

title.description: The session topic — an operator rename or the automatic titler, COMPLETE and untruncated; null when the transcript tail carried neither.

titleSource.description: Provenance of title: custom = explicit rename (authoritative, wins over a later ai-title), ai = automatic titler. null iff title is null.

verdict.description: Only the two verdicts that reach the queue; offer-more and status-only are filtered out by buildInbox.

surface.description: EXACTLY four fields. tabStatus and every other source-surface field are not projected.

actions.description: [{kind:'reply'}] when answerable, [] otherwise. There is no dismiss.
